title: The killing of the chief and Italians hiding in her house
summary: She recalls the day the chief was killed and how her family sheltered three Italians; a song 'Downfall of a Lion' is mentioned.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: No, I don't remember that. Well, you remember who killed the chief, I bet.
You remember when they killed the chief?
I guess so. I remember that.
It was in March. Straight through All-East Street. Straight through? Yeah. It was in March?
Wasn't it in March? Well, I don't remember. Yes, it was. It was, no.
Yeah, because Sydney had been around town.

Sydney would be 65, and Sydney was 63 years ago. Yes, indeed. We had plenty of dagoes home. When they were chasing them, you know, to kill them, on the counter, they killed their chief. They were afraid. So whoever was charitable enough, they were dying of fright, would let them in. We had three at home.
You let them stay in your house, huh?
They were hiding in your house.

Yes, whoever was charitable enough, because one man, all didn't kill that one man. Yes, it was on a Friday in March. Friday, I believe it was. Either Friday or Wednesday. It was very, very windy, that day.

They even have a song about that, but I can't get it. It's called The Downfall of a Lion. And they used to sing that around James Alley, if you know where that is. That's up in the, what, the Third Ward or the Second Ward?
Back to the Third Ward, I think. I don't know. Third Ward. Third Ward, yeah. It's in the battlefield.
